subject: Post-call: Novalytics POC definition + SLO targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Novalytics POC definition + SLO targets

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. High-level recap and proposed next steps below. I captured what I heard and added a couple of clarifying questions.

Quick recap (what we covered)
- Primary use case: automated meeting summarization + extractable action items for enterprise accounts (internal and reseller workflows).
- Target traffic for POC: ~2000 summary requests/day at peak; average prompt length ~1.2k tokens; expected average generation length ~400 tokens.
- Contract constraints: data residency in US + SOC2 evidence requested.

POC success framework (first pass) — please review and flag gaps:
- Latency: median < 350ms for 95% of requests (production-like workload, 512 prompt prefix).
- Throughput: sustain 45 RPS during simulated peak for sustained 10-minute windows.
- Cost: target blended generation cost < $0.007/token in trial (we'll provide quantization + batching guidance).
- Quality: f1-based extract accuracy for action items >= 0.78 on your labeled set (we'll provide eval harness).

Clarifying questions for your team:
1) Can you confirm the canonical dataset for the POC (source location + sample size)?
2) Do you have an existing rubric for "action item" extraction we can use for the eval, or should Redwood build a short labeling guide?
3) Any constraints on rate-limiting or burst policies we should model?

Proposed next steps:
- Internal: Ben to sketch the performance test harness and infra runbook; Monica to share the SOC2 evidence checklist and initial onboarding questionnaire.
- External: Alex / Priya to share a 200-sample extract set and a short note on retention policy by EOD Friday (2025-11-07).
- We’ll follow up with a formal POC charter and a short deck that maps your objectives to measurable gates.

Attachments: I attached a simple metrics template (Novalytics_POC_success_metrics.xlsx) and a diagram request for your networking team (novalytics_network_topology.png).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@novalytics.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Novalytics POC definition + SLO targets

Marissa — appreciate the thorough recap. A few quick notes:
- The 200-sample extract: Priya will export and share by Friday. That will include examples labeled by our CS team (action-item flag + priority).
- For the canonical dataset: we have ~25k internal meeting transcripts. For POC we can provide a 2k sample (anonymized) and a 200-sample labeled subset. Will that be enough for your eval harness?
- On retention: default policy is 90 days for POC artifacts; enterprise contract would extend to 1 year.

On latency and cost targets: your latency goal looks aggressive but reasonable. Curious how you plan to measure the 95th percentile at production-like loads — can you share the test harness outline?

Also — two asks from my side: 1) can you include an expected runbook for a canary rollout (we have strict change windows); 2) provide a preliminary ballpark for monthly cost at the trial scale (assume 2k daily requests).

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product
Novalytics
alex.turner@novalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-06T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Novalytics POC definition + SLO targets

Great — thanks Alex. Yes, 2k anonymized transcripts + the 200 labeled examples are perfect to start. Responses below to your asks and a little more detail on measurement approach.

How we'll measure latency and throughput
- We'll spin a performance harness in your staging VPC that replays requests with the same token distribution you share.
- Measurement windows: 10 x 10-minute runs across the day to capture variance; we’ll report p50, p95, p99 and producer-side queuing.
- For SLO gating we recommend p95 < 350ms and p99 < 900ms for the POC — those map to your product's UX targets.

Canary / rollout runbook (short)
- Canary in staging: start with 5% traffic for 30m -> 25% for 60m -> 100% if no regressions.
- Monitoring: token-level latency, error rates, and cost burn (per-route). Automatic fallback to a smaller model variant on error spike.

Preliminary cost estimate (trial scale, illustrative)
- Based on 2k requests/day x 400 tokens per generation average -> ~800k generation tokens/month.
- With batching/quantization and our suggested runtime settings: estimated billable cost ~ $5,600–$7,200/month (range depends on final batch size and exact quant profile). We’ll refine once we see the real distribution.

Next steps — commits from Redwood team:
- Ben: I’ve asked you to draft the perf harness outline and the infra playbook (due Tue 11/11).
- Monica: please attach SOC2 artifact checklist and the short onboarding questionnaire (if ready).

Alex — if that aligns I’ll prepare a 1-page POC charter and send a calendar invite for a kickoff next week.

—
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-11T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Perf harness outline + infra notes (Novalytics POC)

Alex / Marissa — quick technical note on how we’ll validate the throughput/latency targets.

Planned test components:
- Load generator (k6 + custom token-aware replay) located in Novalytics staging VPC — we use your network to remove cross-region noise.
- Model variants: primary (redwood-1.3b-q4_0) as a cost/perf candidate and fallback (redwood-2-7b) for quality checks.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching with max batch 64, target latency cap 300ms, and prefix-KV cache enabled for repeated meetings.
- Data sanity: we’ll run an initial smoke test with 50 synthetic requests before full runs.

Risks / mitigations:
- If your staging network is behind a strict egress filter, we may ask for temporary exception for load IPs — please loop infra.
- If the labeled set shows low inter-annotator agreement we’ll need to extend labeling or provide a small rubric-driven relabel.

I attached the perf harness sketch as a slide in the shared Drive link. I’ll aim to have a runnable repo and a sample k6 script by EOD Monday (2025-11-17).

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@novalytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-12T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Novalytics POC definition + SLO targets

Marissa / Ben — thanks, that all looks good and thank you for the clear plan. A couple of quick confirmations:
- We can get the 2k anonymized transcripts to you by 11/14.
- Priya confirms staging team can open the temporary egress range for the load IPs you’ll send.
- We’d like one short workshop (30m) during the first week of the POC to align on label definitions for action items — can you propose two time slots next week?

Agreed on the canary cadence. Please send the 1-page POC charter and the perf harness repo link when available. Once the charter is in place we’ll route for internal approval (procurement + security).

Looking forward to kickoff.

—
Alex
